name: Discord

auth.keyHelp: Open your application, go to Bot, press Reset Token and copy it; invite the bot to your server with only View Channels and Read Message History for read-only use.

write.label: Send a message to a channel

tested: mock; real service refused a fake key
notes: Docs moved from discord.com/developers/docs to docs.discord.com/developers (301). Base is https://discord.com/api/v10 (v10 and v9 available; v8 and older deprecated or discontinued; pin the version because the unversioned default is not stated). The bot header is 'Authorization: Bot <token>'. Discord requires a User-Agent of the form 'DiscordBot ($url, $versionNumber)' and may block requests without one with a Cloudflare error; the value here is a placeholder the host must replace with its own URL and version. GET /applications/@me returns the application tied to the bot (id, name, description, owner). GET /users/@me is documented only for OAuth2 (identify scope); the page does not say bot tokens may call it, so it is not used for the test. GET /users/@me/guilds is documented with the guilds OAuth scope and its bot access was not confirmed, so it is left out. GET /guilds/{id}/channels: from 2026-11-16 it will omit channels the bot cannot view. GET /guilds/{id}/members needs the privileged GUILD_MEMBERS intent. Reading message text needs the privileged MESSAGE_CONTENT intent (without it content, embeds, attachments and components come back empty) plus VIEW_CHANNEL and READ_MESSAGE_HISTORY. Send message needs SEND_MESSAGES; content is limited to 2000 characters. Bot permissions are chosen when the bot is invited, so a read-only bot is possible. No official Discord-published MCP server was found (search returned only community projects), so mcp is null.
